glossary.definition: RLHF is the technique AI labs use to make a raw, freshly-trained language model actually behave helpfully and safely. Human reviewers look at pairs of AI responses to the same question and pick the better one, and the model is retrained to produce more answers like the ones humans preferred. Think of it as a talented but very literal new employee, submitted their first drafts to an editor over and over until their instincts started matching what people actually wanted. It's a major reason today's chatbots feel conversational and considerate rather than just spitting out raw predicted text.

items.title: NiCE’s next-generation Cognigy bets the hard part of AI agents is running them, not building them
items.summary: The contact center has been the low-hanging fruit for the artificial intelligence industry. Ask any information technology or business leader what they want to use agentic AI for, and they will say it’s to improve the customer experience, which starts with the contact center. However, to date, the industry has spent the past two years arguing over which AI agent is the smartest. That’s the wrong debate.

items.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
items.summary: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn't sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters . The project, called the "World Product Graph," is meant to make it less likely that shoppers leave Amazon to do their product research on Reddit or Google, and make it more likely shoppers end up at Amazon even if they're searching for a product sold elsewhere. Listing the details of everything for sale everywhere is meant to make Amazon more useful than Reddit for people and AI agents. items.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.summary: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations. It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news.

items.title: Microsoft 365 services slowly come back online after global outage
items.summary: After a lengthy Microsoft 365 outage disrupted business around the globe, Microsoft is now restoring services to its customers. m. ET) on Friday, Nov. 13, Microsoft said that it is seeing broad recovery and stability across its services, although it is still reporting service degradation in Microsoft 365 services that interact with Exchange Online. “Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage.

items.title: Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life
items.summary: Jensen Huang likely left Nvidia more because of risky business practices than anything else, a Wall Street Journal report suggests. At the very least, those practices made him enemies internally. The company offered cloud providers billions in financial guarantees for chip purchases, including a planned $250 billion deal with OpenAI. Interim CEO and then-CFO Colette Kress tried to contain the risk, and Huang reportedly didn't like that.

items.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.summary: LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith. Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday. That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago , led by IVP. LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
items.summary: The company says a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash. Sorry, Margaret, your email is working again. After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page . The outage debacle began around lunchtime on the East Coast on Thursday, with users reporting Outlook outages to the service-tracking website Downdetector just after 12 pm ET.

items.title: Cloud reports measure the wrong thing
items.summary: Flexera’s 2026 State of the Cloud Report agrees with many other cloud reports these days: Cloud is more strategic, cloud is more complex, AI makes everything harder, and better governance is the answer. This report, based on a survey of 753 cloud decision-makers and users, argues that enterprise cloud has entered a “value era” in which organizations are measuring success less by cost savings alone and more by business outcomes. The headline findings are familiar. Flexera says 64% of organizations now use “value delivered to business units” as a metric for cloud progress, up 12 percentage points year over year.

items.title: SoftBank's AI Empire Rests on a Single Asset—And It's Over-Leveraged
items.summary: Last year, SoftBank Group Chairman and CEO Masayoshi Son declared his vision of turning the Japanese technology investment group into the biggest platform provider for “artificial super intelligence”. That required massive and aggressive investments into all spheres of the AI ecosystem, and it’s finally beginning to dent its bottomline. The Japanese investment holding company reported a ¥1.12 trillion ($6.99 billion) net loss for July–September 2026, its first quarterly loss in about two years, after revising orders for power equipment intended for US data centres that resulted in a ¥597.2 billion ($3.80 billion) charge. But that doesn’t seem to be enough.

items.title: ReNew Pledges ₹80,000 Cr for Green Data Centre to Fuel India’s AI Push
items.summary: ReNew Energy Global plans to invest approximately ₹80,000 crore in Andhra Pradesh across data centre infrastructure and clean energy manufacturing. The investment includes a 1 GW green hyperscale data centre in Anakapalli, envisioned to run on renewable energy. The company has allocated ₹67,000 crore for the data centre and ₹11,000 crore for polysilicon and metallurgical silicon manufacturing facilities in Anakapalli and Nellore. ReNew also plans to invest ₹1,500 crore in a permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Rambilli, expected to be commissioned by March 2029.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s scandal-fueled ouster exposes enterprise doubts about AI
items.summary: The Nvidia shakeup probably won't damage the GPU giant, but it highlights risk lurking in the industry as enterprises deal with unclear ROI from AI technology.

items.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
items.summary: ” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. ” But privately, Nvidia representatives working with Foster told the lawmaker that the company could implement them.
